decision: No blocking mathematical issue found in the conditional real-formula lemma. Accepted as an additive static derivation only.
method: Read complete frozen kernel and literal reference as text, verify hashes, and derive the identities symbolically. No importing or evaluating financial, network, differentiation or sampling routines.
reviewed_proofs: For fixed psi, c,p,q,cost are linear in C,P. The boundary numerator is linear while its denominator and B kernels depend only on psi. Thus positive simultaneous nominal scaling gives b, equity and debt degree one. F/G depend only on psi and log(V/b), so F/G and Q,R,x have degree zero.
The default test is preserved because V<=u*b iff V/u<=b. Its E=0,F=G=1,debt=alpha*b/m assignment has the same degrees; value matching and the zero equity asset derivative remain consistent.

Writing kappa=C/P and beta=b(psi,kappa,1) gives b=P*beta. P=exp(rho)/beta and C=kappa*P make b=exp(rho) exactly in the ideal real formula. Dividing equity by b removes the nominal amplitude, so Q/R depend on z-rho and the eight shape parameters.

At fixed shape, Q_rho=-Q_z, R_rho=-R_z and x_rho=-1. Across default, these are statements about the selected C1 Q/R/x observables under the stated joint regularity and bounded continuation first-derivative assumptions, not about raw F/G becoming C1.

At fixed psi, P_kappa=-P*beta_kappa/beta, P_rho=P, C_kappa=P+kappa*P_kappa and C_rho=kappa*P. Their 2x2 determinant is P^2. Adding the unchanged seven-dimensional psi identity block preserves local invertibility on an open valid domain; eight shape plus one boundary coordinate retains nine financial parameters.

The P_* anchor identity follows from the same homogeneity. The anchor interval [20,100] intersect [0.5/kappa,10/kappa] and target B interval [20 beta,100 beta] intersect [0.5 beta/kappa,10 beta/kappa] are correct coupon/principal box restrictions, additional to the remaining financial conditions.
clarifications: The normalized ideal stopping sign H=delta*beta-(1-tax)*kappa+(alpha*beta-1)/m<0 is not the complete finite-epsilon acceptance test. With S=abs(delta*beta)+abs((1-tax)*kappa)+(abs(alpha*beta)+1)/m, the real-expression form of the actual numerical margin is H < -64*epsilon*max(1/P,S). This agrees with the note warning that max(1,scale) breaks arbitrary nominal-scale acceptance invariance.

Closed API box endpoints do not themselves provide a two-sided feasible numerical neighborhood. The ideal local differential change of variables is not a proof that the entire constrained implementation domain is globally trainable.

The same valid financial branch, finite positive beta, open-region C1 assumptions and current hard-domain restrictions remain prerequisites. Global stopping optimality is not established by the local source guard.
